decision_rule: Scope: the 64 stated mining rows that tools/sweep_company_level.py flags (one source page cited as stated by several plants for the same field, quote without the plant's city; OSHA rows removed). Confirmed = the cited passage, directory entry or job requisition names this plant's place or facility (street address, site name, or a plant named in the passage), or the page itself names this plant as the company's only manufacturing site; a passage naming only a city or state counts only under the shared-city / campus rule (consultation 10: no other production site there, or the others within about 1 km doing the same production). Job-board list pages count as site-level when the cited requisition's own location names the site. Corrected = the page states the value only for the company, a division, a two-site pair or another site (corrected_tag inferred, value reworded as company-level where it was not already), or a clause comes from another site. Unreachable only if the source cannot be reached at all.
error_rate_note: Targeted sweep of rows a script pre-flagged as likely company-level, not a random sample: 42/64 = 65.6% is not comparable to the sampled round rates and should not be read as mining's general fact error rate. Of the 42 corrections, 27 are tag-only (the value already said company-level, 'naming both Hartford plants' or 'plant not named'; only the stated tag was wrong), 14 reword a company line in the row value (8 of them also reword a plants.csv field that presented it as the site's own), and 1 (CMI Waverly) keeps the stated tag but replaces a clause about a predecessor at another site. Profiled plants: 9 rows, 6 corrected (PPI Pella 2, Standard Iron Sumner 4), none changing a score or confidence. Base plants: 55 rows, 36 corrected. The 22 confirmed rows are false positives of the script's heuristic (job-board JSON with the requisition's street address, directory entries with each company's own address, articles about one named plant).
repeated_kinds: quote does not support value (42) - one pattern, the one this sweep targets: a company-level (or two-site) page tagged stated at one plant. 27 of the 42 already said company-level or two-site in the value; 14 needed the value reworded as company-level (Rockland Seguin x2, Conn-Weld, Niece Buda, TCI Walnut, Irwin Car, Peters, Ramsey, Simmons x2, Matcor home-page rows x4); 1 clause from another site (CMI 1929 Cedar Rapids). Every quote whose page was reachable was found, except the two Pengo rows, whose Epiroc posting has since been filled. Nothing invented. Apply this file rather than running sweep_company_level.py --apply, which would also retag the 22 confirmed site-level rows.

sweep_company_level.py false-positive pattern: one page that describes several different companies (IAAP directory, Power Curbers careers page) or a job board read as JSON with per-requisition addresses (ADP, UKG, Paycom). Do not run --apply on the mining rows; apply this file instead.
method: Fresh fetch of every cited URL (tools/fetch_page.fetch with_raw=True; browser fallback for ADP, UKG, Paycom), each quote fragment checked against visible text plus raw source; ADP board read through its job-requisitions API from the page context (44 requisitions with requisitionLocations street addresses); MEC UKG board read through LoadSearchResults, all 179 postings paged; Superior contact page fetched to list every Minnesota, Nebraska and New Mexico address; ledger coordinates used for the Bluefield (1.7 km) and Hartford (2.3 km) distances; Wayback availability API for the filled Epiroc posting (snapshot found, fetch reset twice). Rows matched to the sweep list by claim_id and URL prefix; each (claim_id, source_url) pair is unique in evidence.csv and no flagged quote contains the plant's city. No web search used. No ledger file edited.
apply_note: Apply with tools/apply_factcheck.py (rows keyed on claim_id + full source_url, each pair unique in evidence.csv). Do not also run sweep_company_level.py --apply on these rows: it would retag the 22 confirmed site-level rows. plants_csv_value starting 'keep' leaves the field; the second Rockland row says keep because the first (rocklandmfg.com) row carries the reworded field.
